title: Automatic Differentiation
hook: Backprop is one instance of a general trick: autodiff computes exact derivatives of any program by composing the chain rule — the engine inside every deep-learning framework.
key_points: Autodiff computes exact gradients of a function expressed as code, not by hand or finite differences.
Reverse-mode autodiff is backpropagation generalized to arbitrary computation graphs.
Frameworks record each operation, then replay it backward to accumulate gradients.
This is why you write the forward pass and get the backward pass for free.
content_html: Automatic differentiation (autodiff) is the technique that lets a computer compute exact derivatives of a function written as ordinary code. It is neither the messy hand-calculus of a textbook nor the inaccurate finite-difference approximation — it applies the chain rule mechanically to every elementary operation. Backpropagation is the most famous special case, and autodiff is the engine inside PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow.
extra_html:
How it works

As the forward pass runs, the framework records each primitive operation and its inputs into a computation graph. Reverse-mode autodiff then walks that graph backward from the output, multiplying local derivatives via the chain rule and accumulating the gradient for every parameter in a single sweep. Because the cost of the backward pass is proportional to the forward pass, training huge models stays tractable. (Forward-mode autodiff exists too, but reverse-mode wins when you have many parameters and one loss.)

Why it matters

Autodiff is the quiet abstraction that made modern deep learning practical to build. You define only the forward computation; the framework derives the gradients automatically and correctly, no matter how exotic the architecture. That frees researchers to experiment with new layers and losses without re-deriving calculus by hand — turning "how does this train?" from a research project into a one-line loss.backward().

related.title: How Neural Networks Learn: Backpropagation
related.hook: A neural net learns by asking, for every weight, 'how much did you contribute to my mistake?' Backprop answers all of them at once.

flashcards.prompt: What is the relationship between backpropagation and autodiff?

choices.text: Backprop is reverse-mode autodiff applied to neural nets
Backprop is a finite-difference approximation of autodiff
Autodiff is a special case of backpropagation

flashcards.explanation_html: Reverse-mode autodiff is backpropagation generalized to arbitrary computation graphs; backprop is its most famous special case.

flashcards.prompt: How does a framework compute the backward pass for free once you write the forward pass?
flashcards.back_html: It records each primitive operation into a computation graph during the forward pass, then walks it backward applying the chain rule.

flashcards.prompt: Why is reverse-mode autodiff preferred for training large models?

choices.text: It wins when you have many parameters and one loss
It is the only mode that gives exact derivatives
It avoids building a computation graph

flashcards.explanation_html: Reverse-mode wins with many parameters and a single loss; the backward cost stays proportional to the forward pass.
